lessons.crossCurricular: English: listening for detail; Maths: numbers and times
lessons.smsc: Moral and social: attentive listening (iṣghāʾ) shows respect
starter: Retrieval: say '8:30' and '3:15' in Arabic.
Say the Arabic for 'left' and 'right'.
Say 'twenty pounds' and 'five nights'.

teach.heading: Before, during, after
bullets: Use reading time: underline question words
Predict the answer type: number, place, reason
First hearing: gist; second: confirm detail
Never leave a blank: write an answer
teach.note: Per the spec file each extract is heard twice and the first five minutes include reading time. Questions in English at Foundation Section A, with different formats at Higher: check the SAMs. Teach pupils to write short answers (a word or a number) and to listen to the end of the sentence before deciding: speakers often correct themselves (ليس ... بل ...). Practise note-taking with abbreviations in English.

teach.heading: Sounds that trap
teach.note: Say each pair twice. Pupils write which they hear on mini-whiteboards. Then they listen to a full sentence. Teach the habit of checking the number against context (a price, a time, a date). The singular and plural number words may sound similar but the noun and the context disambiguate.

teach.heading: Practice script (teacher reads twice)

quote.text: تَبْدَأُ الرِّحْلَةُ فِي الثَّامِنَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ صَبَاحًا وَلَيْسَ فِي التَّاسِعَةِ. سَيَكُونُ الْجَوُّ بَارِدًا وَلَكِنَّهُ مُشْمِسٌ. اِحْضُرُوا مَعَكُمْ غَدَاءً وَقُبَّعَةً وَخَمْسَةَ جُنَيْهَاتٍ لِلْمَتْحَفِ.
quote.source: Original practice listening script (teacher reads aloud twice)

teach.note: Teacher: read this slowly, twice, at natural pace, with a pause between readings. Do not show it. Pupils answer the questions in the practice section. This is an original script, not an exam extract. Tell pupils that a speaker 'correcting' themselves is a standard trap: the time is 8:30 and NOT 9.

teach.heading: Model: answering a trap question

model.problem: After two hearings: 'What time does the trip start?' (script above)
steps: Listen for the time phrase: فِي الثَّامِنَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ = at half past eight
Notice the correction: وَلَيْسَ فِي التَّاسِعَةِ = and not at nine
Write the answer in English with the time of day: صَبَاحًا = in the morning

teach.note: Show how to record the detail after hearing it. Then the notes to the answer. Emphasise that the speaker says it is not at nine. Pupils then answer the other questions themselves from the second reading.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: What will the weather be like?
check.why: بَارِدًا وَلَكِنَّهُ مُشْمِسٌ = cold but sunny. The others mix the weather words or add details that are not in the script.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A and C are distractors from the script; D is a different item. Ask pupils to show the phrase they heard that rules out nine o'clock.

practice: Listening practice: teacher reads the script twice; answer: (a) time; (b) weather; (c) three things to bring; (d) the amount of money.
Listen to a short extract of a pupil reading numbers and write them as digits.
Compare answers in pairs and say which phrase gave you each answer.
independent: Core: answer the script questions fully in English.
Extend: write your own 40-word listening script with a trap.
Stretch: swap scripts with a partner and answer theirs, then explain the trap.
exit: Write the English for 'وَلَيْسَ فِي التَّاسِعَةِ'.
Give two strategies for the listening paper.
lessons.homework: Listen to a short Arabic news item or recording and write five details in English.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: allow pauses and give a glossary of the script. Stretch: listen to unfamiliar topics at natural speed.

lessons.title: Revision: Higher structures and common errors across the themes
lessons.bigQuestion: Which structures help me reach the top marks, and which errors do I still make?
objectives: Review the main structures across Themes 1 to 5
Identify and correct common errors
Plan a revision route for all four papers
successCriteria: All: use past, present and future accurately
Most: use at least three higher structures with accuracy
Some: correct errors in a paragraph and explain the rule
lessons.crossCurricular: All subjects: revision and self-assessment skills
lessons.smsc: Spiritual and moral: perseverance (ṣabr), planning and reliance on Allah after effort
starter: Retrieval: write one sentence with the past, one with the future.
Say the rule: what ending does a verb take after أَنْ?
Say the rule: what case follows أَنَّ?

teach.heading: Structure bank

head: Structure
Example
English
rows: I used to play every day
I think the weather is hot
he is the man who helps me
if I study I will succeed

teach.note: Pupils use this as a revision checklist. For each structure they write an original sentence on a theme of their choice. Rank: which are secure? Tick, circle or cross. The spec file notes the grammar list (Appendix 2) was not read for this plan, so the teacher should cross-check the structures against the specification's grammar appendix and add any missing items.

teach.heading: The errors I keep making

misconception.wrong: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبٌ لِأَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمُ قَالَ إِنَّ الطِّبُّ مُفِيدٌ
misconception.right: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَكُونَ طَبِيبًا لِأَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ قَالَ إِنَّ الطِّبَّ مُفِيدٌ - the predicate after 'to be' and the nouns after لِأَنَّ / إِنَّ take the accusative

teach.note: Collect five typical errors from the class's own work (anonymised). Put them on the board and ask pupils to correct them and give the rule. These errors are the quickest marks to gain. Ask pupils to keep a personal 'error log' and review it weekly. The rule in each case should be said in a short sentence.

teach.heading: Model: correcting a paragraph

model.problem: Correct three errors: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَدْرُسُ الطِّبَّ لِأَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمُ قَالَ إِنَّ الطِّبَّ مُفِيدَةٌ
steps: Verb after أَنْ must be subjunctive: أَنْ أَدْرُسَ
After لِأَنَّ the noun is accusative: لِأَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ
The adjective must agree with الطِّبَّ (masculine): مُفِيدٌ
model.answer: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَدْرُسَ الطِّبَّ لِأَنَّ الْمُعَلِّمَ قَالَ إِنَّ الطِّبَّ مُفِيدٌ.

teach.note: Do this as a think-aloud. Find the verb and the subject first, then the object, then the adjectives. The errors are chosen from common mistakes in written work. Pupils then correct a partner's paragraph.

teach.heading: Hinge question

check.q: Which sentence has NO error?
check.why: C is correct: كَانَ takes an accusative predicate. A should be الْجَوَّ, B should be أَدْرُسَ and D should be مُعَلِّمًا.

teach.note: Mini-whiteboards. A has the wrong case after أَنَّ; B the wrong mood after أَنْ; D the wrong predicate case. Ask pupils to explain each error in a sentence.

practice: Write one example of each structure in the bank on a theme of your choice.
Correct: أَعْتَقِدُ أَنَّ الْمَطَرُ شَدِيدٌ. / يَجِبُ عَلَيْنَا أَنْ نَسْتَخْدِمُ الْمَاءَ بِحِكْمَةٍ.
Rank your confidence in each structure: secure, nearly, not yet.
independent: Core: write a 90-word paragraph using five structures from the bank.
Extend: swap with a partner and mark each other's error types.
Stretch: write a 120-word answer to a task with every higher structure used correctly.
exit: Correct: لَمْ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
Name your most common error and the rule.
lessons.homework: Make a one-page revision sheet: three structures with example sentences, your top three errors with corrections, and a plan for each paper.
lessons.send: EAL/SEND: give a pre-filled structure bank and an error checklist. Stretch: write a mock paper task on Theme 5 and mark it with the checklist.
